research_query: Does Low-Dose Metformin Extend Lifespan in Non-Diabetic Mammals?
description: Curated benchmark dataset of 15 peer-reviewed studies evaluating the longevity effects of Metformin in healthy non-diabetic animal models with documented dosage and model system confounders.

papers.title: Metformin improves healthspan and lifespan in non-diabetic male mice
papers.abstract_text: We investigated the longevity effects of 0.1% dietary metformin (approx 50 mg/kg/day) initiated in middle-aged male C57BL/6 mice. Metformin treatment significantly extended mean lifespan by 14.2% (p = 0.002) compared to vehicle controls (n = 120). Treated animals exhibited improved physical performance, lower hepatic steatosis, and enhanced insulin sensitivity without apparent nephrotoxicity. Gene expression profiling revealed activation of AMPK and upregulation of antioxidant pathways.

papers.title: High-dose metformin induces renal failure and shortens lifespan in healthy rodents
papers.abstract_text: To determine upper therapeutic thresholds, male C57BL/6 mice were administered 1.0% dietary metformin (approx 250 mg/kg/day) starting at 12 months. Rather than extending longevity, high-dose metformin decreased median lifespan by 11.5% (p = 0.008, n = 90). Histological examination revealed acute tubular necrosis, elevated serum creatinine, and lactic acidosis. We conclude that high-dose metformin exceeds renal clearance capacity, causing metabolic toxicity and shortening lifespan.

papers.title: Longevity extension by metformin in outbred genetically heterogeneous mice
papers.abstract_text: Under the NIA Interventions Testing Program (ITP), genetically heterogeneous male and female mice (UM-HET3, n = 240) were fed 0.1% metformin starting at 9 months. Metformin led to a statistically significant 12.8% increase in median lifespan in male mice (p = 0.004) and a 7.1% increase in female mice. Biomarkers of chronic low-grade inflammation and mTORC1 signaling were significantly suppressed in liver and visceral adipose tissue.

papers.title: Metformin fails to prolong life in non-human primate rhesus macaque cohort
papers.abstract_text: In a 10-year longitudinal trial involving aged rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta, n = 32), daily metformin (25 mg/kg) was evaluated against matched controls. Metformin treatment improved fasting glucose regulation and reduced triglycerides, but failed to show a statistically significant effect on overall survival or maximum lifespan (hazard ratio 0.94, p = 0.62). The difference in longevity observed in short-lived rodents does not translate directly to long-lived primates.

papers.title: Metformin delays age-related functional decline and extends median survival in Fischer 344 rats
papers.abstract_text: Fischer 344 rats (n = 80) receiving low-dose metformin (30 mg/kg/day) demonstrated improved rotarod endurance, preserved neuromuscular junctions, and an 8.6% extension in median lifespan (p = 0.015). Metformin prevented age-associated sarcopenia and reduced systemic IL-6 levels. No adverse gastrointestinal or renal effects were noted at this dosage.

papers.title: In-vitro cellular senescence assay reveals metformin cytotoxicity in primary endothelial cells
papers.abstract_text: Primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) exposed to metformin concentrations above 5 mM displayed mitochondrial fragmentation and decreased replicative capacity (p = 0.003). In-vitro cell culture assays fail to capture systemic hepatic clearance and vascular hormonal feedback observed in intact in-vivo models.

papers.title: Metformin preserves stem cell exhaustion and extends lifespan in short-lived Nothobranchius furzeri
papers.abstract_text: The short-lived turquoise killifish (n = 110) treated with 20 mg/kg metformin in water displayed an 18.1% prolongation in mean survival (p = 0.001). Metformin sustained intestinal epithelial integrity and attenuated neurodegenerative decline, confirming conserved anti-aging mechanisms across vertebrate classes.

papers.title: Normoglycemic aged mice show no survival benefit under intermittent metformin dosing
papers.abstract_text: Intermittent weekly pulse administration of metformin (100 mg/kg twice weekly) in aged female BALB/c mice (n = 64) failed to significantly extend lifespan (p = 0.44). Continuous daily dosing appears necessary to sustain AMPK phosphorylation and downregulate mTORC1, whereas intermittent pulses allow rapid metabolic rebound.

papers.title: Divergent lifespan outcomes between genetically identical cohorts under identical low-dose metformin protocols
papers.abstract_text: Two independent replicates of male C57BL/6J mice (Cohort 1 n = 50, Cohort 2 n = 50) were maintained on identical 50 mg/kg/day metformin diets in pathogen-free vivaria. Cohort 1 demonstrated a 10.4% extension in median lifespan (p = 0.02), whereas Cohort 2 exhibited no significant survival difference (+1.2%, p = 0.78). Microbiome sequencing and environmental logging revealed no identifiable confounder to account for the discrepancy.

papers.title: Low-dose metformin attenuates oxidative lipid peroxidation and prolongs median survival in Swiss albino mice
papers.abstract_text: Swiss albino mice (n = 95) administered 40 mg/kg metformin daily showed a 15.3% increase in median survival (p = 0.001) alongside marked reductions in malondialdehyde and 4-hydroxynonenal in cardiac and brain tissue. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity was elevated by 32%.

papers.title: Comparative cohort analysis of metformin versus rapamycin on healthspan parameters in aged rats
papers.abstract_text: Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 75) evaluated for functional longevity under low-dose metformin (50 mg/kg) showed sustained cardiovascular arterial elasticity and an 11.2% extension in healthy lifespan (p = 0.007). In comparison with rapamycin, metformin exhibited lower immunosuppressive adverse events.

papers.title: Supra-pharmacological metformin causes gut dysbiosis and exacerbates frailty in senescent mice
papers.abstract_text: Administration of 300 mg/kg metformin in 20-month-old DBA/2 mice (n = 55) resulted in a 16.4% reduction in maximum lifespan (p = 0.003). Fecal metagenomic sequencing indicated severe depletion of Akkermansia muciniphila and expansion of pro-inflammatory Enterobacteriaceae, confirming dose-dependent enterotoxicity.

papers.title: Epigenetic clock deceleration and lifespan gains under metformin in wild-derived mice
papers.abstract_text: Using DNA methylation epigenetic clocks, wild-derived mice (n = 80) receiving 50 mg/kg metformin exhibited a 2.4-year biological age deceleration and a 13.9% extension in chronological lifespan (p = 0.002). Methylation changes were concentrated in promoters governing autophagy and DNA double-strand break repair.

papers.title: Evaluating metformin in high-fat diet versus standard chow longevity models
papers.abstract_text: Metformin (60 mg/kg) was tested in both standard chow and high-fat diet (HFD) fed C57BL/6 mice (n = 120). While HFD-fed mice showed a dramatic 22.4% lifespan recovery (p < 0.001), standard chow controls exhibited a modest but statistically significant 7.8% extension (p = 0.03). Metformin provides primary metabolic correction under dietary stress with secondary geroprotective effects under normocaloric feeding.

papers.title: Comprehensive multi-omic benchmark of geroprotective compounds across mammalian aging cohorts
papers.abstract_text: In a cross-consortium lifespan study across 4 distinct mammalian strains (n = 320), metformin at 50 mg/kg achieved an aggregated 11.8% median lifespan increase across rodent lines (p = 0.0008), with single-cell transcriptomics confirming reversal of age-associated chronic inflammatory cascades in liver, kidney, and hypothalamus.
